comment: Synthetic witnesses for docs/expression-contract.md's E series (#823). Every scene is invented: ACME and BRV are not instruments, no figure describes any real book, and nothing here is derived from a user record. A negative scene must fail EXACTLY the assertion it declares -- a witness that fails two is not a witness for either, because it cannot prove the check it names is the one that fired.

scenes.note: The shape references/trade-consequence.md's answer slots describe: judgment body, then one tail block. The unit and denominator qualifiers stay inline (D2); staleness, cash reliability and the unchecked list go to the block.
scenes.answer:
What this buy mainly changes is not your entry price — it is the size of a bet that is already past the line you set. Priced on cost rather than on current market value, ACME goes from 30% to about 38%, and that 38% is measured over the part of your book that carries a classification.

The strongest case the other way attacks those same numbers: cost weights move when the market does, and your largest position being your highest-conviction name is a choice rather than an accident. Your own words — "the drop feels too good to pass up" — describe a price move, and my read is that nothing in them names a change in the business.

Your call: keep this open, decline it, or modify the size — nothing has been executed.

[i] Computed on your recorded book as of the 15th, 45 days old, never reconciled against a broker view.
[i] The negative cash line is a running sum with no anchor behind it, not a real overdraft.
[i] Not checked: liquidity, valuation, tax, or whether the position still suits you.

scenes.note: An answer whose numbers carry no triggered limitation ends at its last judgment. The absence of a block is the rule working, not an omission.
scenes.answer:
Your own rule caps a single name at 20%, and this buy leaves ACME at 12%, so nothing you wrote collides with it. The book stays inside every line you set.

Your call — nothing has been executed.

scenes.note: A non-consider surface inheriting the same placement rules. One triggered limitation, one line.
scenes.answer:
Volatility rose through the week while your heaviest name was already flagged as too large — the two land on the same position, which is what makes it worth a look rather than a headline.

Worth watching next week: whether that name's weight moves at all, and whether the volatility reading holds above where it sat when this review was frozen.

[i] Both readings are the ones frozen with your review, not fresh quotes taken today.

scenes.note: The classic regression: the block is written, then an offer is appended after it, so the disclosures stop being the end of the answer and become a middle section.
